Skattekort must be obtained before first payroll run; delays cause higher withholding tax (50%).
Folkeregisteret address registration must be done within 8 days of establishing residence.
D-number is issued for short stays; fødselsnummer (permanent ID) is issued after 6 months — bank accounts often require the latter.

templates.route_title: Brazil — VITEM V Work Visa / CRNM
templates.employee_summary: Your employer must first obtain work authorisation from Brazil's Ministry of Labour (SINFRE/MTE), which unlocks your VITEM V (temporary worker) visa at the consulate. After arrival, you must register with the Federal Police within 90 days to obtain your CRNM (national migration registration card) and then obtain a CPF (tax ID) with Receita Federal.
templates.hr_summary: Initiate the MTE employer authorisation as the critical path item — this can take 4–8 weeks before the employee can even apply at the consulate. Ensure CRNM and CPF steps are completed within 90 days of arrival to maintain legal status.
templates.internal_notes_hr: VITEM V is the standard route for employed workers. The CRNM replaces the old RNE card. CPF is required for bank accounts, payroll, and any Brazilian contracts. CTPS (Carteira de Trabalho) digital registration with the employer is also required. Private health insurance is strongly recommended as public SUS access for foreigners is limited.
watchouts: Ministry of Labour (MTE/SINFRE) authorisation is the critical path — allow 4–8 weeks before consulate application.
CRNM Federal Police registration must be completed within 90 days of first entry or legal status lapses.
CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas) is required for payroll, bank accounts, and almost all official transactions.
CTPS (digital employment card) must be registered with the employer at hiring.
Private health insurance is strongly recommended; public SUS access for non-citizens can be limited.

templates.route_title: Italy — Nulla Osta / National Visa + Permesso di Soggiorno
templates.employee_summary: Non-EU/EEA nationals require a Nulla Osta (work authorisation) issued by the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione, followed by a National (Type D) visa at the Italian consulate. Within 8 working days of arrival, you must submit a Permesso di Soggiorno (residence permit) application at the Post Office or Questura. EU/EEA nationals need only an Iscrizione anagrafica. All workers need a Codice Fiscale (tax code) and Residenza registration.
templates.hr_summary: Nulla Osta is the critical path item for non-EU/EEA employees — apply via the Sportello Unico as soon as the job offer is confirmed, as processing can take 8–16 weeks. The Permesso di Soggiorno 8-working-day window after arrival is legally strict. EU Blue Card is available for high earners (salary ≥ €32,000/year for 2024).
templates.internal_notes_hr: Italy's Decreto Flussi (annual quota decree) restricts some non-EU work visa categories — confirm the route is open. The Codice Fiscale is required for payroll, contracts, banking, and rental agreements. Permesso di Soggiorno can take 3–6 months to be issued but the kit receipt (ricevuta) is accepted as proof in the meantime.
watchouts: Nulla Osta from the Sportello Unico can take 8–16 weeks — start immediately after job offer is confirmed.
Permesso di Soggiorno application must be submitted within 8 working days of arrival — missing this window creates irregular status.
The kit receipt (ricevuta del kit postale) acts as temporary proof while the Permesso is processed (3–6 months).
Codice Fiscale is required for payroll, contracts, banking, and leases — obtain it as soon as possible.
Decreto Flussi annual quotas may restrict certain non-EU work categories — confirm route availability in advance.

milestones.title: Type D visa granted
milestones.body_employee: Check visa validity. Plan entry date accordingly.
milestones.body_hr: Retain copy; update compliance record; confirm start date.

milestones.title: Arrival & Permesso di Soggiorno kit
milestones.body_employee: Arrive in Italy. Within 8 working days, buy the Permesso di Soggiorno kit at Poste Italiane and submit your application. Keep the ricevuta as proof.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm arrival; monitor 8-day window; support with Poste Italiane visit if needed.

milestones.title: Codice Fiscale, Residenza & healthcare
milestones.body_employee: Obtain Codice Fiscale from Agenzia delle Entrate. Register Residenza at local Comune. Enrol in ASL healthcare.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm Codice Fiscale is on file before payroll run; schedule 3-month check-in.

milestones.title: Permesso di Soggiorno issued & settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Collect Permesso di Soggiorno card (typically 3–6 months after application). Open bank account, finalise rental contract.
milestones.body_hr: File Permesso di Soggiorno copy; update renewal calendar (typically valid 2 years, then renewable).

templates.route_title: Spain — Work & Residence Authorisation / NIE / TIE
templates.employee_summary: Non-EU/EEA nationals require a combined work and residence authorisation (autorización de residencia y trabajo por cuenta ajena) initiated by the employer in Spain, followed by a visa at the Spanish consulate. After arrival, you obtain your NIE (foreigner ID), complete Empadronamiento (municipal registration), and apply for the TIE (residence card). EU/EEA nationals only need NIE, Empadronamiento, and EU registration certificate. All workers need a Social Security number.
templates.hr_summary: The employer must file the work and residence authorisation application in Spain as the critical path step (allow 1–3 months). Ensure NIE, Empadronamiento, and TIE steps are completed promptly after arrival. Social Security number registration must precede payroll.
templates.internal_notes_hr: Non-EU/EEA nationals: the autorización is issued in Spain by the immigration office (Delegación del Gobierno), then the employee collects their visa at the Spanish consulate abroad. NIE is the core identifier used in all Spanish official processes. TIE replaces the old green certificate for non-EU nationals. Highly Qualified Professional (EU Blue Card) route available for salaries ≥ 1.5× average salary.
watchouts: The employer-filed work and residence authorisation can take 1–3 months — start immediately after offer is confirmed.
NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) is required for almost all Spanish official and commercial transactions.
Empadronamiento (municipal registration) is required for healthcare access, school enrolment, and many administrative processes.
TIE application must be submitted within 30 days of entering Spain on the work visa.
Social Security number must be registered before payroll can run — obtain via employer or INSS office.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract
checklist.notes_employee: Required for the work and residence authorisation application.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm contract specifies role, salary, and work location in Spain.

checklist.title: Work and residence authorisation (autorización de residencia y trabajo) application filed
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer files with the Delegación del Gobierno in Spain. Allow 1–3 months.
checklist.notes_hr: Critical path — initiate immediately after offer is signed. Track expediente number.

checklist.title: Work and residence authorisation granted
checklist.notes_employee: Employer receives resolution; you can then apply for the visa at the Spanish consulate.
checklist.notes_hr: Send resolution to employee promptly; consulate step must follow within validity window.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 1 year beyond the intended stay.

checklist.title: Spanish work/residence visa obtained at consulate
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Spanish consulate in your country of residence with the authorisation resolution.
checklist.notes_hr: The visa is typically valid for 90 days entry — must be used within this window.

checklist.title: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) obtained
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the local Policía Nacional comisaría or via consulate. Required for all official and commercial transactions in Spain.
checklist.notes_hr: NIE is the key identifier — payroll, bank accounts, and lease agreements all require it.

checklist.title: Empadronamiento (municipal address registration) completed
checklist.notes_employee: Register at your local Ayuntamiento (town hall) with passport, visa, and rental contract. Required for healthcare and school enrolment.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm registration; needed for healthcare access from day one.

checklist.title: TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) residence card application submitted
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Policía Nacional within 30 days of entering Spain. Bring: passport, visa, NIE, Empadronamiento certificate, photos, and employment contract.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain appointment receipt as interim proof; TIE takes 4–6 weeks to issue.

checklist.title: Social Security number (Número de Afiliación) registered
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer registers you with the INSS (Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social) before your first working day.
checklist.notes_hr: Required before payroll — employer registers affiliation number at INSS.

milestones.title: Kickoff — work and residence authorisation application
milestones.body_employee: HR files the work and residence authorisation with the Delegación del Gobierno in Spain. This is the critical path step.
milestones.body_hr: File autorización de residencia y trabajo immediately — processing can take 1–3 months.

milestones.title: Authorisation granted
milestones.body_employee: HR sends you the resolution. Book your consulate appointment promptly — the resolution has a validity window.
milestones.body_hr: Send resolution to employee; ensure they book consulate within validity window.

milestones.title: Consulate appointment & visa obtained
milestones.body_employee: Visit Spanish consulate with resolution, passport, photos, and supporting documents. Collect visa.
milestones.body_hr: Track visa collection; confirm planned entry date.

milestones.title: Arrival in Spain
milestones.body_employee: Enter Spain. The 30-day TIE application window starts from entry.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival date; set TIE 30-day reminder immediately.

milestones.title: NIE, Empadronamiento & Social Security
milestones.body_employee: Obtain NIE at Policía Nacional. Complete Empadronamiento at Ayuntamiento. Employer registers your Social Security affiliation (INSS).
milestones.body_hr: Confirm NIE and Social Security number on file before first payroll run.

milestones.title: TIE application submitted
milestones.body_employee: Apply for TIE (residence card) at Policía Nacional within 30 days of entry. Retain appointment receipt as interim proof.
milestones.body_hr: File appointment receipt; TIE card typically issued in 4–6 weeks.

milestones.title: TIE received & settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Collect TIE card. Open Spanish bank account. Enrol children in school if applicable. Schedule 3-month check-in.
milestones.body_hr: File TIE copy; update TIE renewal calendar (typically valid 1–2 years, then renewable); confirm payroll and healthcare active.

templates.route_title: Australia — TSS Subclass 482 / Employer Nomination Subclass 186
templates.employee_summary: Your employer nominates you for either a Temporary Skill Shortage (subclass 482) visa or the permanent Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186). Labour Market Testing and, for some occupations, a skills assessment are required before lodgement. After arrival, obtain a Tax File Number (TFN) and enrol in superannuation.
templates.hr_summary: Labour Market Testing must be documented before the nomination is lodged. Confirm occupation eligibility on the MLTSSL/STSOL lists. Subclass 186 (ENS) offers a permanent pathway. Ensure TFN and superannuation are set up before first payroll.
templates.internal_notes_hr: Subclass 482 (TSS) requires Labour Market Testing unless covered by international agreement. Occupation must be on the relevant skilled occupation list. Superannuation is compulsory (currently 11%). Medical examination may be required depending on nationality/occupation.
watchouts: Labour Market Testing (LMT) must be conducted and documented within 12 months before lodging the nomination — advertising requirements apply.
Skills assessments may be required for some occupations — confirm with the relevant assessing authority before starting the process.
Subclass 482 is a temporary visa; align renewal dates with contract length and plan permanent pathway (subclass 186 or 191) early.
TFN must be obtained before payroll — without it, the employer must withhold tax at the highest marginal rate.
Superannuation contributions are compulsory — employer must enrol the employee within 28 days of eligibility.
Visa holders on subclass 482 may only work for the sponsoring employer — any role change requires a new nomination.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract confirming role, salary, and work location
checklist.notes_employee: Required for nomination lodgement.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm role is on eligible occupation list (MLTSSL/STSOL/PMSOL).

checklist.title: Labour Market Testing (LMT) completed and documented
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer must advertise the role and show no suitable Australian worker was available.
checklist.notes_hr: LMT advertising must be within 12 months prior to nomination lodgement — keep records of all ads and applicants.

checklist.title: Skills assessment submitted (if required for occupation)
checklist.notes_employee: Contact the relevant assessing authority for your occupation. Lead time: 4–12 weeks.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm if skills assessment is required for the specific ANZSCO occupation code.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for the intended visa period.

checklist.title: Visa nomination and application lodged with Home Affairs
checklist.notes_employee: Employer lodges the nomination; you then lodge the visa application online.
checklist.notes_hr: Track nomination and visa application reference numbers. Processing: 2–8 months depending on stream.

checklist.title: Visa granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check visa grant notice for conditions, validity dates, and any travel restrictions.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain grant notice; confirm planned entry date and start date.

checklist.title: Tax File Number (TFN) applied for with ATO
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at ato.gov.au or at a Medicare office. Required for payroll and banking.
checklist.notes_hr: Withhold maximum tax rate until TFN is provided — chase promptly after arrival.

checklist.title: Superannuation fund nominated
checklist.notes_employee: You may choose your own fund or use the employer's default. Complete the Standard Choice Form.
checklist.notes_hr: Enrol within 28 days of becoming eligible; SG contributions currently 11%.

checklist.title: Medicare or private health insurance arranged
checklist.notes_employee: Medicare eligibility depends on your nationality and visa type. If not eligible, arrange OSHC (Overseas Student/Worker health cover).
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm Medicare eligibility; some nationalities and visa holders require private OVHC cover.

milestones.title: Kickoff — LMT and nomination preparation
milestones.body_employee: HR begins Labour Market Testing, confirms your occupation is eligible, and prepares the nomination.
milestones.body_hr: Conduct LMT advertising; document all applicants; confirm occupation list eligibility before lodging nomination.

milestones.title: Nomination and visa application lodged
milestones.body_employee: Nomination lodged by HR; you receive an invitation to complete your visa application online.
milestones.body_hr: Track nomination reference; guide employee through online visa application.

milestones.title: Visa granted
milestones.body_employee: Check grant notice for conditions and validity. Plan your travel date accordingly.
milestones.body_hr: Record grant date and visa expiry; align start date.

milestones.title: Arrival in Australia
milestones.body_employee: Enter Australia. Your visa is electronically linked to your passport — no label required.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival date; initiate TFN and superannuation onboarding.

milestones.title: TFN, superannuation & healthcare
milestones.body_employee: Apply for TFN online. Complete the superannuation choice form. Enrol in Medicare or arrange private health cover.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm TFN and super fund on file before first payroll run.

milestones.title: Settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Open Australian bank account. Register with local GP. Organise schooling for children if applicable.
milestones.body_hr: Schedule 3-month and 12-month check-ins; set visa renewal reminder.

templates.employee_summary: Most foreign workers in Canada require an employer-specific work permit. The route is either LMIA-based (employer obtains a positive Labour Market Impact Assessment from ESDC) or LMIA-exempt (e.g. CUSMA/USMCA, Intracompany Transfer, or international agreements). After arrival, obtain a Social Insurance Number (SIN) and enrol in provincial health insurance.
templates.hr_summary: Confirm the correct route: LMIA-based vs LMIA-exempt (CUSMA, ICT, C-11, etc.). LMIA takes 2–5 months — start immediately. LMIA-exempt routes are faster but require the correct legal basis. SIN must be obtained before payroll; provincial health insurance has a 3-month waiting period in most provinces.
templates.internal_notes_hr: LMIA-based: employer must advertise and show no qualified Canadian was available. LMIA-exempt: document the legal basis carefully (e.g. CUSMA profession list, ICT relationship). Intracompany Transfers (C-12) require the employee to have worked abroad for 1 year with the same company. Express Entry PR pathway available in parallel.
watchouts: LMIA processing can take 2–5 months — initiate immediately if LMIA route is required.
Most provinces have a 3-month waiting period for provincial health insurance — arrange private health coverage from day one.
The work permit is employer-specific (tied to the employer and role) — a new work permit is required for role changes.
SIN must be obtained from Service Canada before payroll can run legally.
Open work permits are available for spouses of skilled workers and international students — apply in parallel for dependents.

checklist.title: Work permit route confirmed (LMIA-based or LMIA-exempt)
checklist.notes_employee: HR will confirm whether an LMIA is required based on your role and nationality.
checklist.notes_hr: Review CUSMA profession list, C-12 ICT eligibility, or other LMIA-exempt codes before pursuing LMIA route.

checklist.title: LMIA obtained from ESDC (if required)
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer applies to ESDC. Allow 2–5 months. You will be notified of the outcome.
checklist.notes_hr: Advertise per ESDC requirements; retain all records. Process takes 2–5 months in high-wage stream.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract and offer letter
checklist.notes_employee: Required for work permit application.
checklist.notes_hr: Ensure offer specifies NOC code, wage, hours, and duration.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for the intended work permit period.

checklist.title: Work permit application submitted online or at port of entry
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at ircc.canada.ca or at the port of entry (CUSMA professionals only).
checklist.notes_hr: Track application number; IRCC online processing typically 2–8 weeks for most exemptions.

checklist.title: Work permit granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check permit conditions — it will specify employer, location, and expiry date.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain copy; align start date with permit validity.

checklist.title: Social Insurance Number (SIN) obtained from Service Canada
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at a Service Canada centre with your work permit and passport. Required for payroll and tax filing.
checklist.notes_hr: SIN required before first payroll — chase within first week of arrival.

checklist.title: Provincial health insurance enrolled (or interim private insurance arranged)
checklist.notes_employee: Most provinces have a 3-month waiting period — arrange private international health coverage from day one.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm employer provides interim private health cover for the waiting period.

checklist.title: Canadian bank account opened
checklist.notes_employee: Required for salary deposit. Most major banks allow opening with passport and work permit.
checklist.notes_hr: Required for salary payment; arrange before first pay date.

milestones.title: Route determination & LMIA kick-off (if required)
milestones.body_employee: HR determines the correct work permit route. If LMIA is required, HR begins the ESDC application process.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm route; initiate LMIA if required — allow 2–5 months. For exempt routes, prepare supporting documentation.

milestones.title: LMIA granted / exempt route confirmed
milestones.body_employee: HR provides LMIA confirmation or exempt route documentation. You may now apply for the work permit.
milestones.body_hr: Issue LMIA and offer letter; guide employee through online work permit application.

milestones.title: Work permit application submitted
milestones.body_employee: Apply online at ircc.canada.ca or at the port of entry (for CUSMA professionals).
milestones.body_hr: Track IRCC application reference; prepare for supplemental document requests.

milestones.title: Work permit granted
milestones.body_employee: Check permit conditions, employer, and expiry date. Plan travel date.
milestones.body_hr: Retain copy; confirm start date; arrange private health insurance for 3-month waiting period.

milestones.title: Arrival in Canada
milestones.body_employee: Enter Canada with your work permit approval letter and passport.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival; initiate SIN and banking onboarding immediately.

milestones.title: SIN, provincial health & banking
milestones.body_employee: Obtain SIN at Service Canada. Open a Canadian bank account. Register for provincial health insurance to start the waiting period clock.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm SIN on file before first payroll run; track provincial health waiting period.

milestones.title: Settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Enrol children in school if applicable. Arrange rental contract. Set up provincial health insurance after waiting period.
milestones.body_hr: Schedule 3-month check-in; set work permit renewal reminder.

templates.route_title: Switzerland — Residence & Work Permit (Permit L / B)
templates.employee_summary: Non-EU/EEA nationals require an employer-sponsored residence and work permit (Permit L for stays under 1 year, Permit B for stays of 1–5 years) issued by the cantonal migration office (Migrationsdienst/SMIG). EU/EEA nationals register directly under the Agreement on Free Movement of Persons. Mandatory Swiss health insurance must be arranged within 3 months of arrival.
templates.hr_summary: Non-EU/EEA permits are subject to annual cantonal and federal quotas — confirm availability before making an offer. The cantonal migration authority issues the permit; the employer sponsors it. Health insurance, AHV social security, and commune registration are mandatory post-arrival steps.
templates.internal_notes_hr: Permit B (B-Bewilligung) is the standard annual permit for employed workers; renewable annually. Permit L is for short assignments under 12 months (not renewable). EU/EEA nationals register at the Einwohnerkontrolle with employer confirmation. Non-EU/EEA quota availability should be checked with the canton before offer stage.
watchouts: Non-EU/EEA work permit quotas are limited per canton — check availability before making a job offer.
Mandatory Swiss health insurance (Krankenkasse) must be arranged within 3 months of taking up residence — late enrollment incurs retroactive premiums.
Address registration at the commune (Einwohnerkontrolle) must be completed within 14 days of arrival.
AHV/AVS social security contributions are mandatory and deducted from payroll — employee must receive their AHV number.
Spouses of permit holders need their own permit application — apply in parallel.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract confirming role, salary, and start date
checklist.notes_employee: Required for cantonal permit application.
checklist.notes_hr: Salary must comply with Swiss standard of living; cantonal minimum wage thresholds apply.

checklist.title: Cantonal permit quota availability confirmed (non-EU/EEA)
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer will check with the cantonal migration authority whether a quota is available.
checklist.notes_hr: EU/EEA nationals skip quota check. For non-EU/EEA, confirm quota before offer is extended.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for the intended permit period.

checklist.title: Cantonal migration office permit application submitted
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer files with the cantonal migration office (Migrationsdienst/SMIG). Processing: 4–8 weeks.
checklist.notes_hr: File immediately after quota confirmed. Include contract, diplomas, and employer declaration.

checklist.title: Residence and work permit granted
checklist.notes_employee: You will receive a permit document to collect on arrival or at a Swiss mission.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain permit copy; confirm start date; track permit expiry for renewal.

checklist.title: Address registered at commune (Einwohnerkontrolle)
checklist.notes_employee: Register at your local Einwohnerkontrolle (German CH) or contrôle des habitants (French CH) within 14 days of arrival. Bring passport, permit, rental contract.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm registration — required for AHV enrollment and health insurance.

checklist.title: Mandatory health insurance (Krankenkasse) enrolled
checklist.notes_employee: Arrange basic Swiss health insurance within 3 months of taking up residence. Retroactive premiums apply from first day if late.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm employee has enrolled; check if employer contributes to supplemental insurance.

checklist.title: AHV/AVS social security number received
checklist.notes_employee: Issued automatically via employer payroll registration. Required for pension contributions.
checklist.notes_hr: Register employee with cantonal compensation office; AHV number needed before first payroll.

checklist.title: Swiss bank account opened
checklist.notes_employee: Required for salary. Most banks require permit and commune registration confirmation.
checklist.notes_hr: Required for CHF salary payment.

milestones.title: Quota check & permit application
milestones.body_employee: HR confirms quota availability for your nationality and files the cantonal permit application.
milestones.body_hr: Check quota with canton; initiate permit application immediately — processing 4–8 weeks.

milestones.title: Permit granted
milestones.body_employee: Permit issued. You may now plan your move and travel date.
milestones.body_hr: Issue permit document to employee; confirm start date; set permit renewal reminder.

milestones.title: Arrival & commune registration
milestones.body_employee: Arrive in Switzerland. Register your address at the commune (Einwohnerkontrolle) within 14 days.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm arrival and commune registration; initiate AHV enrollment and health insurance onboarding.

milestones.title: Health insurance & AHV enrollment
milestones.body_employee: Arrange mandatory Krankenkasse health insurance within 3 months. Receive your AHV social security number via employer.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm health insurance enrollment; register AHV number before first payroll.

milestones.title: Settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Open Swiss bank account. Register children in school. Note permit expiry for renewal.
milestones.body_hr: Schedule 3-month check-in; set permit renewal reminder (Permit B renewed annually).

templates.route_title: Hong Kong — Employment Visa (General Employment Policy / Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals)
templates.employee_summary: Foreign nationals require an employment visa from the Hong Kong Immigration Department. The employer sponsors the application under the General Employment Policy (GEP) or a specific admission scheme. After arrival, obtain your Hong Kong Identity Card (HKID) within 30 days and ensure your employer enrolls you in the Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF).
templates.hr_summary: Employment visa applications are employer-sponsored and processed by the HKID Department. Processing: 4–6 weeks. HKID must be obtained within 30 days of arrival. MPF enrollment is mandatory within 60 days of employment commencement. Hong Kong has no personal income tax filing requirement for most employees — salaries tax is assessed by IRD.
templates.internal_notes_hr: GEP requires proof the position cannot be filled locally. Salary should be commensurate with the local market rate. The Quality Migrant Admission Scheme (QMAS) is an alternative for high-talent individuals (points-based, no job offer needed). Dependent visas available for spouses and unmarried children under 18.
watchouts: HKID must be obtained within 30 days of first landing — fines apply for non-compliance.
MPF enrollment is mandatory within 60 days of employment commencement — employer must register and make contributions.
Employment visa is employer-specific — a new visa is required if the employee changes employer.
No general income tax filing for most employees, but a tax return may be issued by IRD — respond within the deadline.
Dependent visa holders may not work without a separate work visa.

checklist.title: Employment offer letter confirming role, salary, and duration
checklist.notes_employee: Required for visa application.
checklist.notes_hr: Demonstrate that the position cannot be filled locally.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 1 month beyond intended stay.

checklist.title: Employment visa application submitted to Hong Kong Immigration Department
checklist.notes_employee: Employer-sponsored; application includes proof of qualifications and employment contract.
checklist.notes_hr: Processing typically 4–6 weeks. Apply online at immd.gov.hk.

checklist.title: Employment visa granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check visa approval letter for conditions and entry instructions.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain copy; confirm start date.

checklist.title: HKID (Hong Kong Identity Card) obtained within 30 days of arrival
checklist.notes_employee: Visit an Immigration Services Centre (ISC) within 30 days of arrival with your passport and visa approval letter.
checklist.notes_hr: Track HKID registration date — mandatory legal requirement.

checklist.title: MPF (Mandatory Provident Fund) enrollment within 60 days
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer registers you with an MPF scheme. Both employer and employee contribute 5% of relevant income.
checklist.notes_hr: Enroll within 60 days of employment commencement. Choose an MPF trustee.

checklist.title: Hong Kong bank account opened
checklist.notes_employee: Requires HKID, employment visa, and employer letter. Required for HKD salary payment.
checklist.notes_hr: Required for payroll — arrange before first pay date.

checklist.title: Tax obligations with IRD noted
checklist.notes_employee: IRD may issue a salaries tax return — respond within 1 month. You are not required to file proactively in most years.
checklist.notes_hr: Inform employee of IRD obligations and tax equalization policy if applicable.

milestones.title: Visa application submitted
milestones.body_employee: Employer submits employment visa application to Immigration Department.
milestones.body_hr: Prepare full application pack including employment contract, qualifications, and employer letter. Processing: 4–6 weeks.

milestones.title: Visa granted
milestones.body_employee: Visa approval letter received. Plan your travel and entry date.
milestones.body_hr: Retain copy; confirm start date; brief employee on HKID 30-day rule.

milestones.title: Arrival & HKID registration
milestones.body_employee: Enter Hong Kong. Register for HKID at an Immigration Services Centre within 30 days.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival date; set HKID 30-day reminder; initiate MPF enrollment.

milestones.title: MPF & banking
milestones.body_employee: Employer enrolls you in MPF. Open Hong Kong bank account for salary payments.
milestones.body_hr: Complete MPF enrollment within 60 days; confirm bank account details for payroll.

milestones.title: Settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Obtain HKID, open bank account. Arrange schooling for children if applicable.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm all registrations; schedule annual visa renewal check-in.

templates.route_title: Japan — Work Visa (Certificate of Eligibility / Engineer / Specialist in Humanities)
templates.employee_summary: Working in Japan requires a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) obtained by your employer from the Regional Immigration Services Bureau, followed by a work visa at the Japanese consulate in your home country. After arrival, you must complete resident registration (Juminhyo) at the municipal office within 14 days and receive your My Number card.
templates.hr_summary: The employer files the COE with MHLW/Immigration — processing takes 1–3 months. The most common visa categories are 'Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services' and 'Highly Skilled Professional' (HSP points). Juminhyo registration and My Number enrollment are mandatory within 14 days of establishing residence.
templates.internal_notes_hr: COE is valid for 3 months — employee must use it within this window to obtain the visa and enter Japan. The Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) visa offers a points-based accelerated path to permanent residency. Dependent (Kazoku Taizai) visas required for family members. Residence card (Zairyū Card) issued at port of entry for stays over 90 days.
watchouts: Certificate of Eligibility (COE) processing takes 1–3 months — initiate the moment the offer is confirmed.
COE is valid for only 3 months from issuance — employee must obtain the visa and enter Japan within this window.
Juminhyo (resident registration) must be completed at the municipal office within 14 days of establishing residence.
My Number (Individual Number) is required for tax filing, payroll withholding, and social insurance enrollment.
Social insurance (Shakai Hoken: health + pension) enrollment is mandatory for employees and deducted from payroll.
Residence card (Zairyū Card) is issued at the airport for stays over 90 days — carry it at all times.

checklist.title: Employment contract signed confirming role and start date
checklist.notes_employee: Required for COE application.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm job category aligns with COE visa category (Engineer/Specialist, Highly Skilled, etc.).

checklist.title: Certificate of Eligibility (COE) obtained from Regional Immigration Services Bureau
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer applies to the Immigration Services Bureau in Japan. Processing: 1–3 months. You must enter Japan within 3 months of COE issuance.
checklist.notes_hr: Critical path — file immediately after offer is confirmed. Retain original COE for employee.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for the intended visa period.

checklist.title: Work visa application submitted at Japanese consulate
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at the Japanese consulate in your country of residence with COE, passport, and photos.
checklist.notes_hr: Lead time varies by consulate — book immediately after COE receipt.

checklist.title: Work visa granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check visa sticker validity and permitted activities. Enter Japan before COE expiry.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain visa copy; confirm entry date.

checklist.title: Juminhyo (resident registration) at municipal office within 14 days
checklist.notes_employee: Register at your local city hall (Shiyakusho/Kuyakusho) within 14 days of establishing residence. Bring residence card, passport, and rental contract.
checklist.notes_hr: Juminhyo is required for My Number notification and bank accounts.

checklist.title: My Number (Individual Number) notification received
checklist.notes_employee: Delivered by post to your registered address after Juminhyo. Required for tax and social insurance.
checklist.notes_hr: Obtain My Number from employee for payroll tax withholding and social insurance.

checklist.title: Social insurance (Shakai Hoken) enrolled via employer
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer enrols you in health insurance (Kenko Hoken) and pension (Kosei Nenkin) from day one.
checklist.notes_hr: Mandatory for employees — deducted from payroll; employer contributes equal amount.

checklist.title: Japanese bank account opened
checklist.notes_employee: Requires residence card and Juminhyo. Required for salary in JPY.
checklist.notes_hr: Required for payroll — arrange within first 2 weeks.

milestones.title: Kickoff — COE application
milestones.body_employee: HR applies for the Certificate of Eligibility at the Regional Immigration Services Bureau.
milestones.body_hr: File COE immediately — processing takes 1–3 months. COE is valid for 3 months from issuance.

milestones.title: COE issued
milestones.body_employee: COE received. HR sends the original to you for the consulate visa application.
milestones.body_hr: Issue original COE; book consulate appointment immediately — must enter Japan within 3 months.

milestones.title: Consulate visa application & grant
milestones.body_employee: Apply at Japanese consulate with COE, passport, and photos. Collect visa.
milestones.body_hr: Track visa application; confirm planned entry date.

milestones.title: Arrival in Japan
milestones.body_employee: Enter Japan. Residence card (Zairyū Card) issued at port of entry. Carry it at all times.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival date; set Juminhyo 14-day reminder.

milestones.title: Juminhyo & My Number
milestones.body_employee: Register at city hall within 14 days. Receive My Number notification by post.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm Juminhyo registration; obtain My Number for payroll and social insurance.

milestones.title: Social insurance & settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Employer enrolls you in Shakai Hoken (health + pension). Open Japanese bank account.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm Shakai Hoken enrollment; confirm bank account for payroll; schedule 3-month check-in.

templates.route_title: Netherlands — Highly Skilled Migrant Permit (Kennismigrant) / IND
templates.employee_summary: The Highly Skilled Migrant (Kennismigrant) permit is the main route for non-EU/EEA skilled workers in the Netherlands. Your employer — a recognised IND sponsor — files the application; the residence permit is typically issued within 2 weeks. EU/EEA nationals have free movement rights and only need to register at the municipality. All residents need a BSN (citizen service number) and mandatory Dutch health insurance.
templates.hr_summary: The employer must be a recognised IND sponsor (register separately if not). The Kennismigrant salary threshold (€70,200+/year for 30+ years old, or €51,826 for under 30 in 2025 — check current rates) must be met. The 30% ruling may provide a tax advantage for incoming skilled workers. BSN is issued at the municipality on arrival and is mandatory before payroll.
templates.internal_notes_hr: IND processing for Kennismigrant: typically 2 weeks once application is complete. 30% ruling application should be filed within 4 months of first employment in NL. EU Blue Card is an alternative for high-salary roles. Spouse of Kennismigrant holder receives an unrestricted work permit automatically. Dutch health insurance (basisverzekering) must be arranged within 4 months of registration.
watchouts: The employer must be a recognised IND sponsor before the Kennismigrant permit can be filed — register early if not already a sponsor.
Salary threshold for the Kennismigrant permit must be met — verify current IND thresholds (updated annually).
BSN (Burgerservicenummer) must be obtained before payroll can be processed legally.
Mandatory Dutch health insurance (basisverzekering) must be arranged within 4 months of registering as a resident.
The 30% tax ruling provides significant tax relief for incoming workers — apply within 4 months of first employment.
DigiD (Dutch digital identity) is required for online government services — apply as early as possible.

checklist.title: Employer confirmed as recognised IND sponsor
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer must be registered as a recognised sponsor with the IND before filing your permit.
checklist.notes_hr: Check IND sponsor status at ind.nl. If not yet registered, allow 4–6 weeks to become a recognised sponsor.

checklist.title: Signed employment contract meeting Kennismigrant salary threshold
checklist.notes_employee: Salary must meet the IND annual threshold (check current rates at ind.nl).
checklist.notes_hr: Verify salary threshold meets current year requirement; threshold is updated annually.

checklist.title: Kennismigrant permit application submitted to IND
checklist.notes_employee: Employer files online via the IND portal. Processing: typically 2 weeks for recognised sponsors.
checklist.notes_hr: File as soon as contract is signed. Track IND reference number.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for the permit duration.

checklist.title: Residence permit (verblijfsvergunning) granted
checklist.notes_employee: Permit sticker issued at the Dutch mission in your home country (non-EEA nationals) or at IND in NL.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm collection method — IND will advise.

checklist.title: BSN (Burgerservicenummer) obtained at municipality
checklist.notes_employee: Register at the local municipality (gemeente) with passport, residence permit, and rental contract. BSN is issued immediately or within a few days.
checklist.notes_hr: BSN is required before payroll can run — chase immediately after arrival.

checklist.title: Mandatory Dutch health insurance (basisverzekering) enrolled
checklist.notes_employee: Arrange through a Dutch insurer (Zorgverzekeraar) within 4 months of registering as a resident. Coverage is retroactive to registration date.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm enrollment; check if employer provides collective supplemental insurance.

checklist.title: DigiD applied for
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at digid.nl — required for online government services (tax, healthcare registration, DigiD app).
checklist.notes_hr: Strongly recommended for the 30% ruling application and other government interactions.

checklist.title: 30% ruling application submitted (if eligible)
checklist.notes_employee: If eligible, the 30% ruling allows 30% of your salary to be paid tax-free. Apply within 4 months of first employment.
checklist.notes_hr: 30% ruling can be significant — file jointly with employee within 4 months of start date.

milestones.title: IND sponsor confirmation & application
milestones.body_employee: Employer confirms IND sponsor status and files Kennismigrant permit application.
milestones.body_hr: Verify IND sponsor status; file Kennismigrant application immediately after contract is signed. Processing: ~2 weeks.

milestones.title: Residence permit granted
milestones.body_employee: Permit granted. Collect from Dutch mission (non-EEA) or IND in NL.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm collection; brief employee on BSN and health insurance steps.

milestones.title: Arrival & BSN registration
milestones.body_employee: Arrive in the Netherlands. Register at the municipality (gemeente) to obtain your BSN.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival; initiate BSN onboarding and health insurance enrollment.

milestones.title: BSN, health insurance & DigiD
milestones.body_employee: Obtain BSN at gemeente. Arrange basisverzekering health insurance within 4 months. Apply for DigiD.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm BSN on file before first payroll; file 30% ruling within 4 months of start.

milestones.title: 30% ruling & settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: 30% ruling filed (if eligible). Open Dutch bank account. Arrange schooling for children if applicable.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm 30% ruling filed; schedule 3-month and annual permit renewal check-ins.

templates.route_title: UAE — Employment Entry Permit / Residence Visa / Emirates ID
templates.employee_summary: Working in the UAE requires an Employment Entry Permit from MOHRE (Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation), followed by a mandatory medical fitness test, a residence visa stamped in your passport by GDRFA (General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs), and an Emirates ID from the ICP (Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security).
templates.hr_summary: The employer initiates the process by obtaining the Employment Entry Permit. The employee then enters the UAE, passes the medical fitness test, and the residence visa is stamped. Emirates ID is applied for alongside the residence visa application. MOHRE work permit (labour card) must be issued. The entire process takes 4–8 weeks from entry permit to active residence visa.
templates.internal_notes_hr: UAE has a 2-year renewable residence visa for most employees (3 or 5 years for highly skilled under Golden Visa). Health insurance is mandatory by law and is the employer's responsibility in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. No income tax in UAE. End-of-Service Gratuity (EOSG) must be accrued for all employees. DIFC and ADGM operate under separate common law jurisdictions.
watchouts: The Employment Entry Permit must be obtained before the employee enters the UAE — they cannot legally work without it.
Mandatory medical fitness test (HIV, tuberculosis, hepatitis tests) must be passed — some conditions result in visa refusal.
Emirates ID must be applied for alongside the residence visa — it is the primary identification document in UAE.
UAE mandatory health insurance is the employer's legal responsibility in Dubai and Abu Dhabi — must be arranged from day one.
MOHRE work permit must be issued and aligned with the residence visa — the employee cannot be on payroll without both.
Dependents require separate sponsored residence visas — income threshold requirements apply.

checklist.title: Employment offer / contract signed
checklist.notes_employee: Required for MOHRE entry permit application.
checklist.notes_hr: Contract must be attested and meet MOHRE standard — use the Tadbeer standard contract template.

checklist.title: Employment Entry Permit (EEP) obtained from MOHRE
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer obtains the EEP online. You cannot legally work until this is obtained.
checklist.notes_hr: Apply via MOHRE/MOHAP portal. EEP is valid for 60 days from issuance. Critical path item.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 6 months. Passport is held during residence visa stamping.

checklist.title: Entry into UAE on employment entry permit
checklist.notes_employee: Enter UAE using the entry permit (not a tourist visa). Arrange arrival with HR.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm employee enters on the correct permit; tourist visa entry is invalid for employment.

checklist.title: Medical fitness test completed
checklist.notes_employee: Blood test and chest X-ray at an accredited UAE medical facility. Usually results within 1–2 days.
checklist.notes_hr: Failing the fitness test will void the visa process — confirm employee health before initiating.

checklist.title: UAE residence visa stamped in passport
checklist.notes_employee: Employer submits residence visa application to GDRFA. Passport held for 3–7 days for stamping.
checklist.notes_hr: Apply via GDRFA immediately after medical clearance. Issue Emirates ID application in parallel.

checklist.title: Emirates ID applied for and received
checklist.notes_employee: Apply at an ICP service centre or via the UAEPASS app. Emirates ID issued within 5–10 working days.
checklist.notes_hr: Emirates ID is the primary document for all UAE services and contracts.

checklist.title: MOHRE work permit (labour card) issued
checklist.notes_employee: Issued by MOHRE alongside the residence visa. Required for lawful employment.
checklist.notes_hr: File MOHRE work permit application aligned with residence visa timeline.

checklist.title: Mandatory health insurance arranged
checklist.notes_employee: UAE law requires your employer to provide health insurance in Dubai and Abu Dhabi from day one.
checklist.notes_hr: Mandatory for employers in Dubai (all employees) and Abu Dhabi (all residents). Arrange before first working day.

milestones.title: Kickoff — Employment Entry Permit
milestones.body_employee: HR obtains the Employment Entry Permit from MOHRE. You must enter UAE using this permit.
milestones.body_hr: Apply via MOHRE portal immediately after contract is signed. EEP valid 60 days — do not delay entry.

milestones.title: Arrival & medical fitness test
milestones.body_employee: Enter UAE on entry permit. Complete mandatory medical fitness test at an accredited facility.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival; book medical test on arrival day if possible; retain medical clearance certificate.

milestones.title: Residence visa & Emirates ID
milestones.body_employee: Employer submits residence visa application. Passport held 3–7 days. Emirates ID application submitted in parallel.
milestones.body_hr: Apply to GDRFA for residence visa and ICP for Emirates ID simultaneously. Provide interim copy of entry permit as ID.

milestones.title: Residence visa stamped & work permit issued
milestones.body_employee: Collect stamped passport. Receive Emirates ID (5–10 working days after application).
milestones.body_hr: Confirm MOHRE work permit issued alongside visa. Update HR system with visa/permit expiry dates.

milestones.title: Settle-in & banking
milestones.body_employee: Open UAE bank account with Emirates ID and residence visa. Arrange accommodation. Enrol dependents if applicable.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm health insurance active; schedule visa renewal reminder (2 years); confirm end-of-service gratuity accrual starts.

templates.route_title: South Africa — Critical Skills Work Visa / General Work Visa
templates.employee_summary: Non-citizens working in South Africa require a work visa. The Critical Skills Work Visa is available for occupations on the DoL Critical Skills List (no job offer required if skilled). The General Work Visa requires a Labour Market Test confirming no suitable South African candidate was available. Foreign qualifications must be evaluated by SAQA. After arrival, register with SARS for a tax number.
templates.hr_summary: Visa route depends on whether the occupation appears on the DTIC/DoL Critical Skills List. The General Work Visa requires the employer to conduct and document a Labour Market Test via the Department of Employment and Labour. Intracompany Transfer (ICT) visas are available for multinationals. Processing typically takes 4–8 weeks at a VFS centre.
templates.internal_notes_hr: Critical Skills Work Visa: valid for 3–5 years, renewable; no formal job offer needed but proof of qualification and critical skills required. General Work Visa: employer must prove no suitable SA/permanent resident candidate available. ICT: employee must have worked for the same employer for 6 months and have skills not available in SA. Biometric data collected at a VFS Global centre. Police clearance certificate required.
watchouts: SAQA foreign qualification evaluation takes 4–6 weeks — initiate early as it is required for most visa categories.
Police clearance certificate from every country of residence for 12+ months in the past 5 years is required — allow 4–8 weeks.
General Work Visa requires Labour Market Testing proof — employer must advertise and document search for a suitable SA candidate.
Visa processing at VFS can take 4–8 weeks — submit well in advance of the planned start date.
SARS registration is required for tax compliance — must be completed before employment begins.
Private health insurance (medical aid) is strongly recommended — public hospitals have very long waiting times.

checklist.title: Visa type determined (Critical Skills, General Work, or ICT)
checklist.notes_employee: HR will advise on which visa category applies to your occupation and circumstances.
checklist.notes_hr: Check DTIC/DoL Critical Skills List. If not on the list, proceed with General Work Visa and arrange Labour Market Test.

checklist.title: SAQA foreign qualification evaluation submitted
checklist.notes_employee: Submit your foreign qualification documents to SAQA (saqa.org.za). Processing: 4–6 weeks.
checklist.notes_hr: SAQA evaluation is required for most work visa categories. Initiate as early as possible.

checklist.title: Police clearance certificate(s) obtained
checklist.notes_employee: Required from every country you have lived in for 12+ months in the past 5 years. Allow 4–8 weeks.
checklist.notes_hr: International police clearances take time — initiate in parallel with SAQA evaluation.

checklist.title: Labour Market Test completed (General Work Visa only)
checklist.notes_employee: Your employer must advertise the role and show no suitable South African candidate was found.
checklist.notes_hr: Document all advertising and applicant responses. Obtain a 'no objection' letter from the Dept of Employment and Labour.

checklist.title: Valid passport (all travellers)
checklist.notes_employee: Must be valid for at least 30 days beyond the intended visa validity.

checklist.title: Work visa application submitted at VFS Global / SA mission
checklist.notes_employee: Submit full application pack at VFS Global: passport, SAQA evaluation, police clearance, medical certificate, photos, and employment contract.
checklist.notes_hr: Track VFS reference; processing 4–8 weeks. Prepare for supplemental document requests.

checklist.title: Work visa granted
checklist.notes_employee: Check visa validity dates and conditions.
checklist.notes_hr: Retain copy; align start date; set renewal reminder.

checklist.title: SARS tax registration completed
checklist.notes_employee: Register with SARS at a SARS branch or via eFiling. Obtain a South African tax number.
checklist.notes_hr: Tax number required before payroll; employer must register employee for PAYE.

checklist.title: Private health insurance (medical aid) arranged
checklist.notes_employee: Public healthcare has long wait times — private medical aid scheme (Discovery, Medihelp, etc.) is strongly recommended.
checklist.notes_hr: Confirm employer medical aid scheme inclusion; arrange from first working day.

milestones.title: SAQA evaluation, police clearance & LMT
milestones.body_employee: Submit SAQA qualification evaluation. Obtain police clearances from all relevant countries. HR initiates Labour Market Test if required.
milestones.body_hr: Run SAQA, police clearance, and LMT in parallel — allow 4–8 weeks.

milestones.title: Full document pack compiled
milestones.body_employee: All documents gathered: SAQA evaluation, police clearances, medical certificate, passport, photos, employment contract.
milestones.body_hr: Review document pack for completeness before VFS submission.

milestones.title: Work visa application submitted at VFS
milestones.body_employee: Attend VFS Global appointment with full document pack. Biometric data collected.
milestones.body_hr: Track VFS reference; processing 4–8 weeks; prepare for supplemental requests.

milestones.title: Work visa granted
milestones.body_employee: Check visa conditions. Plan travel date.
milestones.body_hr: Retain visa copy; confirm start date; set renewal reminder.

milestones.title: Arrival in South Africa
milestones.body_employee: Enter South Africa. Retain your passport entry stamp.
milestones.body_hr: Log arrival; initiate SARS registration and banking onboarding.

milestones.title: SARS registration & banking
milestones.body_employee: Register with SARS for a tax number (eFiling or SARS branch). Open a South African bank account.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm SARS number before first payroll run; ensure PAYE registration.

milestones.title: Settle-in complete
milestones.body_employee: Arrange private medical aid. Enrol children in school if applicable. Obtain a South African driving licence if needed.
milestones.body_hr: Confirm medical aid active; schedule 3-month check-in; set visa renewal reminder.
